title: 1hrcm1c
The Incident of the Parchment (Thursday of Calamity) and the Death of the Prophet
hook: The Prophet said, "Let me write for you a document so that you will not go astray." The pen stopped before the right of the Ahl al-Bayt was written.
scenes.0.text: In his farewell days the Prophet put the young Usama b. Zayd at the head of the army that was to go to Balqa in the direction of Syria. The army assembled at Jurf. Some people objected to the commander being so young. The first dispute of the farewell days arose here.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: ulks7y
Usama b. Zayd
scenes.0.art.actors.2.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.1.text: At Jurf the objections grew. The army was delayed. The Prophet, whose illness had worsened, went up to the pulpit and answered those who objected. His order was still in force. Even so, the army did not set out.
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.2.text: When the illness grew very heavy, the Prophet turned to those in his room. "Come, let me write for you a document so that you will never go astray after me," he said. He asked for this so that the community would not go astray after him. He also wanted to have written on paper the standing proclaimed for **Imam Ali** at Ghadir.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.3.text: A dispute broke out in the Prophet's room. The saying attributed to Umar was this: "Pain has overcome the Prophet. The Book of God is enough for us." Some wanted the document to be written. Some wanted this saying to be upheld. The noise blocked the writing.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.4.text: When the noise in the room grew, the Prophet said, "Get up." The document was not written. Ibn Abbas, remembering this day, would weep: "The real calamity is that the dispute and the noise came between the Prophet and that document." On that day the writing was prevented. This obstacle later led to **Imam Ali**'s right being set aside at the Saqifa.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: 1q0thws
Ibn Abbas
scenes.5.text: The same report relates three bequests. The first is this: expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula. The second is this: host the delegations that come. The narrator says he forgot the third. Those who love the Prophet never learned this forgotten third bequest. This gap remained with them.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.6.text: The Prophet died on a Monday in Rabi' al-Awwal 11. **Imam Ali** was at his bedside. Imam Ali, whose hand had been raised at Ghadir, closed the Prophet's eyes at that hour.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.6.art.actors.1.label: rrckkf
Aisha
scenes.7.text: When the news of the death was heard in Medina, the city was thrown into confusion. Umar at first did not accept the death. Abu Bakr announced the situation to the people. **Imam Ali** and the Banu Hashim began the funeral preparations. On one side there were those who wept. On the other side there were those who went to the Saqifa.
scenes.7.art.actors.1.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.7.art.actors.2.label: p9t1xw
Abu Bakr
scenes.7.art.actors.3.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
sunni.0.says: The Prophet wishes to have a document written; the saying "pain has overcome him, the Book of God is enough for us", the noise, and Ibn Abbas's "calamity" sentence.
sunni.1.says: The report of the same event; Ibn Abbas weeps.
sunni.2.says: Three bequests: expel the polytheists, host the delegations; the narrator says he forgot the third.
sunni.3.says: "Come, let me write for you a document so that you will not go astray"; the dispute in the setting and the Prophet saying "Get up".
sunni.4.says: The preparation of Usama's army, the objections, and the dispatch of the army in the time of Abu Bakr. (The citations are relayed from WikiShia; the primary texts were not opened.)
sunni.5.says: The preparation of the army and the objections.
sunni.6.says: At the Prophet's death, Umar not accepting the death at first and Abu Bakr announcing the situation.
shia.0.says: A Shia treatise in which the matter of Usama's army is treated from the standpoint of kalam. For the opposing interpretation, Jahiz, al-Uthmaniyya pp. 146-147 is mentioned.
shia.1.says: The report that the Prophet cursed those who did not join the army appears in Shia sources; it is not confirmed by a sound Sunni chain. It should not be given as a definitive statement.
disputes.0.title: 10zjtqb
What was to be written?
disputes.0.sunni: There is no report stating the content of the document; because of the dispute, the document was not written. In the Sunni reading, Umar wished not to tire the sick Prophet and recalled the sufficiency of the Qur'an.
disputes.0.shia: There is no report stating the content of the document; because of the dispute, the document was not written. In the Shia reading, this request is understood as a farewell recalling Imam Ali's standing; this is an inference.
disputes.1.title: 1skgrcg
Usama's army
disputes.1.sunni: The Prophet made the young Usama commander; objections arose, and the movement was delayed. In the Sunni reading, this is a preparation made after Mu'ta, and Abu Bakr later sent the army out.
disputes.1.shia: The Prophet made the young Usama commander; objections arose, and the movement was delayed. In the Shia reading, the army is remembered for taking the leading Companions out of Medina; the report of the curse appears only in Shia books and is not confirmed by a sound Sunni chain.
questions.0: The Prophet had asked for a document "so that you would not go astray." How does his desire to protect his community connect for you with love for the Ahl al-Bayt?
questions.1: Ibn Abbas would weep when remembering this day. What do you think a heart that loves the Prophet notices in this weeping?
questions.2: At Ghadir the Book and the Ahl al-Bayt were entrusted together. How does reading the request for a document on the last day close to this trust deepen your love?
questions.3: The content of the document is not in the reports. What does reading the Prophet's "so that you will not go astray" with calm and with love for the Ahl al-Bayt open up for you?
summary: Bukhari and Muslim report that the Prophet said, "Let me write for you a document so that you will not go astray," and that the document was not written because of the dispute in the room (Bukhari, Sahih, no. 114; Muslim, Sahih, no. 1637a). In the Shia reading, this farewell request is remembered with love for the Ahl al-Bayt and for Imam Ali's standing.
key: The last testament the Prophet wanted written
notes.0: Before his death the Prophet said «let me write for you a document so that you will not go astray» (Bukhari, Muslim).
notes.1: A dispute broke out in the room and the document was not written.
notes.2: Ibn Abbas would call this day «the real calamity».
notes.3: The Prophet died on a Monday in Rabi' al-Awwal 11 AH.
notes.4: This is read as a testament wanting to have Imam Ali's standing written.
